# Quality principles

The standard the weekly review job audits CShells against. Each principle came out of a finding in the baseline audit of 2026-10-10 (see #209). Change this file by PR; the review job reads the version on `main`.

Principles marked *Proposed* are not enforced yet. The review job may cite them but must not file new issues based on them alone.

1. **Defaults never disappear silently.** Customizing one aspect (a lambda, an assembly, a routing option) must add to the zero-config behavior, not replace it; any replacement must be an explicitly named opt-out such as `ClearAssemblies()`. *Rationale:* `AddShells(configure)` and `WithWebRouting` both drop defaults today, which is the most likely "nothing works" moment for a new user.
2. **Every public knob has an observable effect and a test that proves it.** A parameter, return type or option that can be set but is ignored is a bug. *Rationale:* resolver `order:` arguments, `MapShells()` conventions and the FluentValidation validator all compile and do nothing.
3. **One mechanism per concern.** There is one way to order resolvers, one way to configure a feature, one entry point per host shape and one teardown-ordering model; a second mechanism needs a written reason. *Rationale:* three ordering mechanisms and four feature-configuration paths conflicted with each other.
4. **Single-consumer capabilities live with their consumer.** *(Proposed; pending the maintainer decision in #178.)* A seam whose only implementation serves one downstream host belongs in that host's repo, or in an opt-in package, until a second consumer appears. *Rationale:* build leases, the activation runner, the activation 2PC and the Nuplane adapter grew core by 17% for Foundation.Host.
5. **The Abstractions packages hold feature-author contracts only.** Host orchestration, routing internals and plumbing go in implementation packages, internal by default. *Rationale:* `CShells.Abstractions` ships about 30 host-only types to every feature library.
6. **Internal by default.** A type becomes public only when a documented user scenario needs it; tests use `InternalsVisibleTo`, not public test hooks. *Rationale:* about 30 plumbing types and several test-only methods (e.g. `DynamicShellEndpointDataSource.Clear`) are frozen into the API.
7. **One word per concept, one concept per word.** New public vocabulary has to be added to [GLOSSARY.md](GLOSSARY.md), and any synonym it replaces is retired in the same PR. *Rationale:* active/settled/committed/published/verified/returned all mean one thing, and "generation" means three.
8. **The public state model is honest.** If an API says `Active`, the generation is committed and routable; there are no invisible sub-states that need a second interface to observe. *Rationale:* `ISettledShellRegistry` exists only because `GetActive` can return an uncommitted generation.
9. **Unknown or mismatched configuration fails loudly.** Configuration whose effect is silently nil (a mismatched routing path, header names that disagree, an unknown feature name, an array/map shape mix) throws or logs at Error with a fix hint. *Rationale:* several routing and naming mistakes today only log a warning and produce 404s.
10. **Every code snippet in docs compiles against the current API.** Each feature has exactly one documentation home (the wiki), and a rename PR must grep the docs and XML comments. *Rationale:* about 21 references to renamed or removed APIs survive across four doc sets.
11. **No release can ship an unrestorable package.** Packable projects may depend only on packages available from nuget.org, and NU5104 is treated as an error. *Rationale:* `CShells.Nuplane` pins a feedz-only prerelease and is in the publish list.
12. **Tests assert caller-observable behavior through shared helpers.** No reflection "shape" tests, auto-property tests or internal-counter assertions; use one shared `TestShellHost`, logger and registry stub; synchronize with gates, not sleeps. *Rationale:* there are five copies of TestHost, seven capturing loggers, sleep-based drain tests and about 30 filler tests.
13. **Each behavior is specified in one test location.** Table-driven Theories go at the lowest level that can observe the behavior, and integration tests cover only what the unit level cannot. *Rationale:* feature-entry parsing, the lifecycle planner, the dependency resolver and drain are each asserted in 3–6 places.
14. **Code and tests never cite spec IDs.** Names and comments state the behavior or link an ADR; FR-/SC-/US- numbers and review-bot tags are banned. *Rationale:* FR numbers restart in each of 25 specs, so they are ambiguous.
15. **Design history is short ADRs, not live specs.** *(Proposed; pending the maintainer decision in #191.)* A spec folder exists only while its PR is open; durable decisions become 30–50 line ADRs. *Rationale:* 23.4k lines of mostly "Draft" specs describe removed types and mislead agents.
